grade_rationale.text: Afanasyev records the fever-sisters and their cures among Russians, Little-Russians (малоруссы), White-Russians (Бѣлоруссы) and Czechs, and ascribes the Sisinius charm to a Bulgarian priest, so the verified peoples_regions name five peoples.
Afanasyev's account is one source although he works from many manuscripts and collections: he prints the charm as a composite text corrected from several copies.
Ralston independently records that Russian peasants believe a witch's drink can carry the "Fever-Sisters" into a victim; the passage does not cite or quote Afanasyev.
The second source supports only the Russians, and only through one passage whose identification of the Fever-Sisters with the tryasavitsy is flagged; every other people rests on Afanasyev alone.
